provenance.source: IRC s. 1 and s. 63; IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 inflation adjustments); Tax Foundation 2026 federal and state bracket tables; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, United States
provenance.notes: 2026 federal brackets and the USD 16,100 standard deduction were read from the Tax Foundation's summary of Rev. Proc. 2025-32 on 31 August 2026. State brackets came from the Tax Foundation 2026 state table. FICA figures came from PwC and are 2025 values.

verificationTodo: socialSecurity.wageBase is the 2025 figure of USD 176,100 carried forward. Confirm the 2026 Social Security wage base with the SSA before relying on any high-income result.
Confirm the 2026 state brackets, standard deductions and exemptions against each state revenue department.
Single filers only. Confirm nothing in Rev. Proc. 2025-32 changes the single-filer figures used here.
omissions: Only the single filing status is modelled. Married filing jointly, head of household and married filing separately are out of scope, and they change the answer substantially.
Itemised deductions, the SALT deduction cap, the child tax credit, the earned income tax credit and the qualified business income deduction are not modelled.
The alternative minimum tax, the net investment income tax and local city income taxes (including New York City) are not modelled.
State treatment of retirement contributions varies and is not modelled separately from the federal treatment.

federalBrackets.note: Single filer. The 10% and 12% bands received a larger inflation adjustment for 2026 than the bands above them.

standardDeduction.note: Single filer. Taken instead of itemising; this app always takes the standard deduction.

socialSecurity.note: Social Security stops at the wage base; Medicare never does. The extra 0.9% Medicare tax above the threshold is charged on the employee alone, with no employer match.

scale.legalRef: California Revenue and Taxation Code s. 17041
scale.note: Nine brackets and the highest top rate of any state, including the 1% mental health services surcharge above USD 1,000,000.
New York City residents pay a further city income tax on top of this, which is not modelled.
A single flat rate, constitutionally required. Illinois grants a personal exemption rather than a standard deduction.
Texas levies no individual income tax at all. Only the federal computation applies.

inputSchema.label: Gross wages (per month)
inputSchema.help: Gross pay before deductions, month by month. Social Security tax stops once your wages pass the annual wage base, so the month you cross it changes your paycheck.

inputSchema.label: Income tax withheld (per month)
inputSchema.help: Federal plus state income tax withheld from each paycheck, not FICA. Used only for the refund comparison.

inputSchema.label: Traditional 401(k) or 403(b) contributions
inputSchema.help: Pre-tax contributions reduce your taxable income but NOT your Social Security and Medicare wages. A Roth contribution reduces neither, so do not enter one here.

inputSchema.label: Health savings account contributions
inputSchema.help: Contributions made through payroll reduce taxable income and, unlike a 401(k), also reduce Social Security and Medicare wages. This app applies the income tax effect only.
